usage: floss [-h] [-H] [-n MIN_LENGTH]
             [--no {static,stack,tight,decoded} [{static,stack,tight,decoded} ...]]
             [--only {static,stack,tight,decoded} [{static,stack,tight,decoded} ...]]
             [-f {auto,pe,sc32,sc64}] [--language {go,rust,dotnet,none}] [-l]
             [--functions FUNCTIONS [FUNCTIONS ...]] [--disable-progress]
             [--signatures SIGNATURES] [-L] [--version] [-j] [-v] [-d] [-q]
             [--color {auto,always,never}]
             sample

The FLARE team's open-source tool to extract ALL strings from malware.
  floss v3.1.1-0-g3cd3ee6 - https://github.com/mandiant/flare-floss/

FLOSS extracts the following string types:
 1. static strings:  "regular" ASCII and UTF-16LE strings
 2. stack strings:   strings constructed on the stack at run-time
 3. tight strings:   special form of stack strings, decoded on the stack
 4. decoded strings: strings decoded in a function

Language-specific strings:
 1. Go:   strings from binaries written in Go
 2. Rust: strings from binaries written in Rust

positional arguments:
  sample                path to sample to analyze

optional arguments:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -H                    show advanced options and exit
  -n MIN_LENGTH, --minimum-length MIN_LENGTH
                        minimum string length

analysis arguments:
  --no {static,stack,tight,decoded} [{static,stack,tight,decoded} ...]
                        do not extract specified string type(s)
  --only {static,stack,tight,decoded} [{static,stack,tight,decoded} ...]
                        only extract specified string type(s)

advanced arguments:
  -f {auto,pe,sc32,sc64}, --format {auto,pe,sc32,sc64}
                        select sample format, auto: (default) detect file type
                        automatically, pe: Windows PE file, sc32: 32-bit
                        shellcode, sc64: 64-bit shellcode
  --language {go,rust,dotnet,none}
                        use language-specific string extraction, auto-detect
                        language by default, disable using 'none'
  -l, --load            load from existing FLOSS results document
  --functions FUNCTIONS [FUNCTIONS ...]
                        only analyze the specified functions, hex-encoded like
                        0x401000, space-separate multiple functions
  --disable-progress    disable all progress bars
  --signatures SIGNATURES
                        path to .sig/.pat file or directory used to identify
                        library functions, use embedded signatures by default
  -L, --large-file      allow processing files larger than 16 MB
  --version             show program's version number and exit

rendering arguments:
  -j, --json            emit JSON instead of text
  -v, --verbose         enable verbose results, e.g. including function
                        offsets (does not affect JSON output)

logging arguments:
  -d, --debug           enable debugging output on STDERR, specify multiple
                        times to increase verbosity
  -q, --quiet           disable all status output on STDOUT except fatal
                        errors
  --color {auto,always,never}
                        enable ANSI color codes in results, default: only
                        during interactive session

examples:
  extract all strings from 32-bit shellcode
    floss -f sc32 shellcode.bin

  only decode strings from the specified functions
    floss --functions 0x401000 0x401100 suspicious.exe

  extract strings from a binary written in Go (if automatic language identification fails)
    floss --language go program.exe
